svg.title: Why one antenna cannot give two heart rates
svg.desc: Two people with heartbeats at 62 and 78 bpm. On a single-antenna 20 MHz Wi-Fi link both fall into one range bin of about 7.5 m with no angle, so the receiver sees one summed waveform and cannot tell whose beat it is. A MIMO radar or many-antenna system puts each person in a separate range/angle cell and recovers two clean traces, 62 and 78. Research separates people first (radar: up to 16 people with two 79 GHz radars, preprint; Wi-Fi: 3 people with about 18 antennas, SpaceBeat 2024). No ESP32-class result found. Heart rates 62 and 78 bpm are illustrative, not measured.
